blocks.content: While running water shapes landforms primarily through hydraulic action forming V-shaped valleys, moving ice carves deep U-shaped troughs through plucking and abrasion.

rows: Hydraulic action, attrition, solution, vertical downcutting
Plucking (quarrying) and abrasion by moving ice mass
Hanging Valleys above main valley floor (Discordant)
Alluvial fans, natural levees, oxbow lakes, deltas

items: Hanging valleys, formed where smaller tributary glaciers join a deeper main trough, are frequently tested landforms in UPSC and State PSC exams.
Distinct depositional contrasts: Drumlins (basket of eggs topography) belong to glacial landscapes, while Oxbow Lakes belong to mature river stages.
Cirques represent armchair-shaped steep-walled hollows carved at glacier heads.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Glaciers carve steep-sided, flat-floored U-shaped valleys, whereas rivers produce sharp V-shaped valleys through vertical downcutting.
Glacial erosion proceeds mainly through plucking and abrasion, forming features like cirques, arêtes, horns, and hanging valleys.
Fluvial erosion occurs via hydraulic action, abrasion, attrition, and solution, forming features such as waterfalls, meanders, and canyons.
Glacial depositional features include moraines, drumlins, eskers, and till plains, while fluvial deposition creates alluvial fans, levees, and deltas.
